A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe the same STELA study, including Appendices A–G. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual watermarking experiments, detection and perplexity results, ablations, and supplementary robustness analyses in Section 6 and Appendices D and F.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, including Tables 2–3 and Figures 2–6. Results retained from v1 still qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain identical POS-context entropy estimation, adaptive watermark insertion, and weighted detection procedures, including Algorithms 1–3.

E1.justification: The reference corpora and evaluation coverage are unchanged: English WritingPrompts story continuation, Chinese THUCNews news continuation, Korean Oscar web-text continuation, and English synonym-substitution attacks.

E2.justification: KGW, SWEET, EWD, and MorphMark remain the evaluated comparators in Table 2 and Figure 2. No comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the same 500 evaluation instances per language, models, prompting, watermark calibration, and detection/perplexity metrics. Appendix D retains the same WordNet substitution protocol and attack intensities.

E4.justification: The POS-context-length ablation, tagset-granularity comparison, word-category signal decomposition, and synonym-attack analysis are identical in Sections 6.2–6.4 and Appendices D and F.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Figure 2's perplexity distributions. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings match, including Tables 2–3 and Figures 2–6. For example, Llama-3.2/STELA's Korean TPR and Best F1 remain 0.950 and 0.954 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and their mathematical reasoning are identical, including normalized POS-context entropy and the weighted detection statistic's null expectation and variance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about linguistic adaptation, detection without model logits, and detection performance across English, Chinese, and Korean.

C2.justification: Interpretations of linguistic mechanisms and robustness are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning tagging errors, perplexity-only quality evaluation, corpus-domain mismatch, and typological and low-resource coverage.

D1.justification: The MarkLLM implementation, POS taggers, hyperparameters, strength-calibration rule, pseudocode, and code-access statement are identical. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to existing watermarking methods and the claimed novelty remain identical.

P1.justification: Only the first-page marginal stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 10 October 2025 to v2 dated 6 April 2026. All paper prose, terminology, headings, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, algorithm displays, captions, and placement are identical. Pages 2–16 render pixel-identically; page 1 differs only in the lettering of the existing version/date stamp, without a layout change.

improvement.justification: Only the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The scientific content, empirical evidence, exposition, reproducibility information, and appendices are identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
